title: Was Zhou Yu Really Angered to Death by Zhuge Liang? The Histories Tell a Different Last Journey
description:
The Romance of the Three Kingdoms gave us an unforgettable death scene: "Zhuge Liang angers Zhou Yu three times" and "Since Heaven made Yu, why did it also make Liang?" Yet the last journey recorded in Zhou Yu's biography in the Records of the Three Kingdoms is different: Sun Quan approves a plan to take Shu, Zhou Yu goes back to Jiangling to prepare, and on the way he dies of illness at Baqiu. Lu Su's biography and the Jiangbiao Zhuan, quoted in Pei Songzhi's annotations, preserve two versions of the sickbed letter in which he recommends Lu Su. Neither names the illness, and there is no evidence that turns an old arrow wound or anger into the cause of death.

This episode keeps the fighting and deathbed records from around 210 apart from chapters 51 and 54–57 of the novel. The cute illustrations are AI-generated narrative sketches, not reconstructions of anyone's appearance, wounds or real battlefields. Sources checked: 2026-10-19.

chapters.pack-for-west: Zhou Yu brings Sun Quan a plan to march west
chapters.same-age: After Sun Ce dies, Zhou Yu serves Sun Quan
chapters.given-command: Sun Quan sends Zhou Yu; Cao Ren still holds Jiangling
chapters.right-rib: Hit by an arrow, he still tours the camp
chapters.liu-takes-jingzhou: Zhou Yu urges holding Liu Bei, then taking Shu
chapters.illness-appears: Zhou Yu falls ill on the road and recommends Lu Su
chapters.novel-obstacles: The novel sends Zhuge Liang's letter to block him

s04001.text: In 210, Zhou Yu laid out a plan for Sun Quan: march the army west.

s04002.text: Will Sun Quan approve the trip west? How far can Zhou Yu go?

s04003.text: Cao Ren still held Jiangling. What would fighting him cost Zhou Yu?

s04004.text: A later novel has a letter from Zhuge Liang catch him.

s04005.text: On the road, a memorial goes to Sun Quan. Who gets the army after?

s04006.text: How do history and the novel tell this last journey?

s04007.text: Back when Sun Ce was set to cross east, Zhou Yu led troops to Liyang to meet him.

s04008.text: Sun Ce died. Zhou Yu marched to Wu to mourn.

s04009.text: As Central Protector, he and Zhang Zhao aided new ruler Sun Quan.

s04010.text: In 208, Cao Cao's army closed in along the Yangtze.

s04011.text: Liu Cong gave up, and Jingzhou's navy fell to Cao Cao. Would Sun Quan yield too?

s04012.text: In Sun Quan's camp, some urged surrender; others, a fight.

s04013.text: The surrender side said the Yangtze alone could no longer stop Cao.

s04014.text: Zhou Yu urged war: could northern troops in boats really fight a long river war?

s04015.text: He added: the northerners came far, new to the climate; disease was a risk.

s04016.text: He asked Sun Quan for 30,000 elite men to meet Cao at Xiakou.

s04017.text: Who would lead Sun Quan's army?

s04018.text: Sun Quan gave command to Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu.

s04019.text: After Red Cliffs Cao Cao went north, leaving Cao Ren in Jiangling.

s04020.text: Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu faced Cao Ren across the river; no battle yet.

s04021.text: Pei cites the Wu Lu: Cao Ren held much grain in Jiangling.

s04022.text: Stalemate. Who did Zhou Yu send to Yiling first?

s04023.text: He sent Gan Ning, and Cao Ren besieged him.

s04024.text: Gan Ning sought aid; Zhou Yu had to choose how.

s04025.text: He left Ling Tong behind, as Lü Meng advised.

s04026.text: He and Lü Meng marched to Gan Ning's siege.

s04027.text: Siege lifted, he crossed to camp on the north bank.

s04028.text: A battle was set; Zhou Yu rode up to the front himself.

s04029.text: There, a stray arrow struck Zhou Yu in the right side.

s04030.text: The Records call it grave; he went back to rest.

s04031.text: Hearing Zhou Yu was laid up, Cao Ren formed his ranks.

s04032.text: But his biography says he got up.

s04033.text: He toured the camp, rallying the men.

s04034.text: Cao Ren left. Sun Quan made him Lieutenant General and Nanjun governor.

s04035.text: After the arrow he'll travel again. Do his sickbed writings mention it?

s04036.text: Still at Jiangling after the war, he kept advising Sun Quan.

s04037.text: Beyond Jiangling was Jingzhou's new head. How would Zhou Yu handle him?

s04038.text: That man was Liu Bei, now Governor of Jingzhou as General of the Left.

s04039.text: He came to see Sun Quan; Zhou Yu sent a memorial.

s04040.text: Keep Liu Bei in Wu, he urged, away from his troops.

s04041.text: Mindful of Cao Cao in the north and fearing Liu Bei was hard to control, Sun Quan refused.

s04042.text: Then Zhou Yu sent a new war plan. Where would it strike?

s04043.text: Meeting Sun Quan again, he asked to go west and take Yizhou.

s04044.text: Liu Zhang of Yizhou was then pressed by Zhang Lu.

s04045.text: Cao Cao, just beaten, can't fight soon, he said.

s04046.text: He'd go west with Sun Yu, General of Vehement Might.

s04047.text: First take Shu, then Zhang Lu.

s04048.text: Sun Yu would then hold the conquered land.

s04049.text: With Sun Quan he'd hit Xiangyang, pressing Cao north.

s04050.text: Sun Quan said yes. Remember that trip west at the start?

s04051.text: Zhou Yu went back to Jiangling to pack, then set off west.

s04052.text: Once on the road, what stopped him?

s04053.text: Lu Su's biography says Zhou Yu fell gravely ill, already on the road.

s04054.text: His sickbed memorial begins: war still rages, and it troubles him day and night.

s04055.text: He urges Sun Quan: prepare for dangers ahead to be at peace.

s04056.text: It says Cao Cao remains a foe and the border isn't secure.

s04057.text: Liu Bei is near, at Gong'an; the lines almost touch.

s04058.text: Locals aren't won over; someone must reassure them.

s04059.text: He asks Sun Quan to let Lu Su take over his post.

s04060.text: Lu Su was no surprise: Zhou Yu had backed him early. Which talent now?

s04061.text: He judged Lu Su shrewd enough to take on the job.

s04062.text: At the end, he even mentions the day of his own death.

s04063.text: Pei cites a Jiangbiao Zhuan letter. What does it add?

s04064.text: There he falls suddenly ill en route; treatment fails.

s04065.text: It goes on: all who live must die, and a short life is not what he regrets.

s04066.text: His real regret: the Shu and Xiangyang plan never happened.

s04067.text: Pei Songzhi says the letters match in sense, not wording. Can we find the illness?

s04069.text: His biography ends it in four characters: "died of illness at Baqiu."

s04070.text: He was 36. Would Sun Quan accept the memorial recommending Lu Su?

s04071.text: Remember the Nanjun arrow? Not given as the cause; no proof of an old wound.

s04072.text: Sun Quan wore plain mourning; those around him grieved too.

s04073.text: When the coffin came home, Sun Quan met it at Wuhu.

s04074.text: Sun Quan also covered the cost of the return.

s04075.text: Pei's notes quote Sun Quan: Gongjin could aid a king. Now whom can I rely on?

s04076.text: Remember that memorial? Sun Quan made Lu Su Colonel of Martial Vigor, with Zhou Yu's troops.

s04077.text: Cheng Pu became governor of Nanjun.

s04078.text: Lu Su got Zhou Yu's 4,000-plus men and his four fief counties.

s04079.text: Lu Su camped at Jiangling, later moving the army to Lukou.

s04080.text: In the novel, who wants to stop his trip west?

s04081.text: In chapter 57 of the Romance, Zhuge Liang sends a letter. What does it say?

s04082.text: It says Yizhou is rugged, its people strong, supply lines long and hard.

s04083.text: Weak as Liu Zhang is, it says, he can hold Yizhou. And whom must Jiangdong watch?

s04084.text: It also warns: Cao Cao, beaten at Red Cliffs, wants revenge; with Jiangdong empty, he may strike again.

s04085.text: After reading, the novel's Zhou Yu sighs deeply.

s04086.text: He writes to Sun Quan, then leaves his men last orders.

s04087.text: He tells his men he never repaid Sun Quan as he wished, and asks them to serve the Marquis of Wu and finish the task.

s04088.text: The novel: he faints, then wakes crying, "Having made Yu, why Liang?"

s04090.text: Zhou Yu's biography has no such cry.

s04091.text: No checkable surviving text blames Zhuge Liang for his illness.

s04092.text: To see Three Kingdoms legends against the sources, subscribe.
